title: Overprotection and Weak Pawns
subtitle: The Surplus Defense of Strategically Decisive Points
summary: Nimzowitsch's most famous and misunderstood concept: why overprotecting strong central points radiates energy across the board and frees defenders for explosive counterattacks.
aphorism: Overprotection is not mere defense; it is the deliberate accumulation of force around a vital strong point to give your entire army elastic freedom.
attribution: 100th Anniversary Centenary Edition. Newly authored prose and interactive studies inspired by Aron Nimzowitsch (1925).

body.historicalContext: Nimzowitsch argued that strong points (such as an advanced pawn on e5 or d5) deserve multiple surplus defenders. By overprotecting, you create an unshakeable fortress that anchors your entire position.

sections.title: The Meaning of Surplus Defense
sections.markdown:
**[[overprotection|Overprotection]]** means defending a critical strong point (like **e5** or **d4**) with more pieces than immediately required to meet enemy attacks.

Why do this? Because an overprotected square:
1. Cannot be undermined by sudden enemy tactics.
2. Anchors your spatial advantage.
3. Allows any single defender to detach and launch an attack elsewhere without worrying that the strong point will collapse!

moves.comment: White pushes the pawn to the anchor square.
Developing the bishop to overprotect e5.
Black attempts to challenge the anchor.
White takes en passant, opening lines for the overprotecting artillery.

drills.title: Add Surplus Protection
drills.markdown: Your e5 pawn is the anchor of your position. Bring your bishop to d3 to add another layer of overprotection.

hints.text: Move your light-squared bishop from e2 to d3.

feedback.correct: Superb! e5 is now thoroughly overprotected, anchoring your kingside initiative.
feedback.wrong: Place the bishop on d3 to support the e5 pawn.
